findings.authorizedBy: Compression, with the CTD-0012 rewrite as the authorized part.
findings.diagnosis: The two nevers are a pair of absolute refusals stated without a conjunction, which is how an invariant is written. Joined by or they become alternatives. The semicolon in may open doors; may never close the door holds a permission and a prohibition in one sentence so the asymmetry is visible, and but flattens it into an ordinary contrast. Choose if is also a real quantifier: whether presupposes that a choice will be made, if allows the answer to be never.

findings.diagnosis: Rooted in the present is a temporal claim and it pairs with built carefully over time as a contrast: the human root exists now, the measurement does not. Rooted in presence makes it a claim about the layer's subject matter, which the chapter already states, and destroys the contrast the second half depends on. The subtitle is set in single asterisks, which the importer's heading regex does not match, so this is prose rather than a structural label.

The whole CTD-0012 correction in label and prose.

The colon before the two nevers, the paired refusals without a conjunction, the semicolon in the doors sentence, choose if, tradeable, the not-X-but-Y in the currency gloss, and the subtitle's rooted in the present.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, both voice cards, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required, and this section extends the CTD-0012 lesson in a way the chapter version did not. A recorded decision can be carried by a section label as well as by prose, and a label is a route. Restoring the baseline label here would have reopened a high-severity terminology item and broken a public link in the same edit.
